The IIMCS method is an extension of the Mahalanobis Classification System (MCS) and Integrated Mahalanobis Classification System (IMCS) to address the challenges of measurement uncertainty.
The IIMCS employs Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO) to filter out the resonant frequencies that contribute most to the information in the system.
The IIMCS runs the BPSO optimization multiple times (N1) to identify the most reliable features based on their frequency of occurrence.
The case study was conducted on 232 equiaxed nickel alloy first-stage turbine blades, of which 193 were healthy and 39 were defective.
The defective turbine blades contained various types of defects, including microstructural changes, airfoil cracking, intergranular erosion, thin walls, and service wear.
Vibrant Corporation conducted vibration testing of the turbine blades in the frequency range of [3, 38] kHz using Process Compensated Resonance Testing (PCRT) techniques.
A total of 15 resonant frequencies (f1 to f15) were identified from the vibration response of the turbine blades for further analysis.
31 repeated measurements were performed on the nominal turbine blades to assess the potential measurement uncertainty or repeatability.
The use of the optimal subset of features (f2, f4, f14, f15) significantly reduced the margin of the Interval Mahalanobis Distance (IMD) values.
The IIMCS method achieved a classification accuracy of 97.85% on the testing dataset, with only 2 misclassifications out of 232 blades.
The classification reliability indicator 'r' provided by the IIMCS method ranges from -1 to 1, indicating the confidence level of the classification results.
The Monte Carlo Method (MCM) is used in the IIMCS framework to propagate the measurement uncertainty into the Mahalanobis distance space.
The IIMCS method aims to provide a more robust classification system compared to previous approaches like MCS and IMCS by accounting for measurement uncertainty.

The IIMCS method integrates the concept of Interval Mahalanobis Distance (IMD) into the classification scheme to improve the classification procedure and provide an indicator for classification reliability.
The IIMCS method is demonstrated in an experimental case study of an equiaxed nickel alloy first-stage turbine blade, showing satisfactory performance.
